amendments.because: An audit on screen found the real cause: every refresh rebuilds each view, and for an unfinished item the data always differs because it holds running time counters; the section itself closes only through a key press after the jump or a reload
amendments.done_when: After a refresh, a person reading a plan or an item keeps their place and every section they opened, on the board, the full item page and the drawer.

done_when: With a plan open on the full item page, the For the builders section open, the view scrolled far down and text selected, three board refreshes leave the scroll position, the open section, the selection and the same page element; the loading line never shows over a plan that is already on screen; the Releases page keeps its open file and its scroll; the first screen keeps the scroll of its long list; and the full item page opens from the data the page already holds.

known.reason: Human accepted the remaining finding: The owner accepts it as a known issue: when the plan's text really changes above the reader's place, that part is drawn again; it is rare

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A teammate adds a paragraph before the open For the builders section while text inside it is selected. The plan renderer places that paragraph before the details element (src/forge/board_app/markdown.js:94–107), but the positional patch at src/forge/board_app/app.js:40–48 replaces the old details element with the paragraph and appends a new details element. The selection and original section element are lost.
Case: normal use - A merged fix adds a known issue for a file sorted before the open file. Releases sorts the rows at src/forge/board_app/releases.js:157–176; the positional patch keeps the open details element at its old position but changes it to a different file, leaving the original file closed.
Case: normal use - The last sign-off question is answered while a first-screen list is open. The optional sign-off section disappears (src/forge/nextstep.py:117–135 and src/forge/board_app/now.js:239–245), so positional matching replaces the work region containing the list and loses its scroll.
